SK2005 Do not mutate a copy of a readonly struct field

A void struct method that directly writes an instance field is called through readonly field storage.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

Calling a mutating struct method through a readonly field can modify a defensive copy and discard that change. The rule requires same-file evidence of a direct instance-field assignment or increment, rather than treating every non-readonly method as mutating.

Example

Instead of:

readonly Counter counter; void M() { counter.Increment(); } // Increment directly writes Counter's instance state.

Write:

// Choose mutable storage, an immutable replacement API, or an explicit local copy according to intent.

When it does not fire

The catalogue's ambiguous mutable-struct/readonly-field entry is implemented as lost mutation through readonly storage, not a ban on readonly fields inside mutable structs. Only direct readonly field receivers and non-readonly void source struct methods with a top-level assignment/increment/decrement of an instance field are supported. Constructors and init accessors of the field's declaring type, readonly members/types, read-only methods, reference types, extensions, metadata/other-file method bodies, conditional methods, expression trees, nested/conditional writes, properties and in parameters are excluded. This is report-only: removing readonly or changing an API needs author intent.
